lost_facts.assertion: test_r2.py::test_failure_behavior__bad_roles_and_a_bad_tokenizer_abort_the_batch_and_write_no_report -- 'bad roles abort: expected an exception, none raised'. format_batch([GOOD, TOO_LONG, bad_roles], FakeTokenizer()) must raise InvalidRoleSequenceError and leave self.last_report unchanged; the shipped code returned normally instead.
lost_facts.evidence: Shipped data_formatter.py (transcript lines 4850-4906): format_batch's per-example try/except is `except TokenizerCapabilityError: raise` then `except EncodingError: dropped_indices.append(index); continue`. InvalidRoleSequenceError IS a subclass of EncodingError (declared at line 77 of the ticket spec and confirmed in the agent's own encoding.py at ~line 4470-4600), so it falls into the generic EncodingError branch and is silently absorbed as a drop rather than propagating. The agent's own Analysis at line 4843 states the design explicitly: 'skip row-level failures (InvalidRoleSequenceError, ExampleTooLongError)... let config-level failures (TokenizerCapabilityError) abort' -- this is a verbatim restatement of the herring g9.r2.h-role-row read at line 3039/3045 ('Length and role sequence are row problems...those get counted and skipped'). The reversal that retracts exactly this sentence, g9.r2.rev3 ('and yes this is me contradicting myself...that half of it was wrong and im dropping it. only the over-long ones are row problems'), sits as a wiki-page-comment on docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md and was never fetched: its title and body use generic 'row/skip/raise/builder' vocabulary with no overlap against any of the 8 wiki search queries the agent ran (finetune, encoding, tinker, fireworks, tokenizer, training, 'chat template', curator), and the agent never enumerated the docs/engineering book to find pages by title alone.

search_strategy: Chat: dumped whole Mattermost channels to files (/tmp/ch1.txt, /tmp/ch2.txt, etc via /tmp/mm.py, /tmp/mmch.py) then grepped for term clusters ('EncodingReport|encoding|format_batch|supervised|window|role|last_report|tru...', 'ALLOWED_ROLES unknown_role non_alternating role sequence bytes'); this recovered most chat clues but some individual channel-day exchanges fell outside the dumped page ranges and were missed even when the channel overall was visited (e.g. g9.r2.l16, g9.r2.g9-tuple-return-2). Mail: fetched by explicit numeric message-id ranges (/tmp/mailb.py 116 117 118 124 128 144) rather than a full mailbox search, so entire threads whose ids fell outside the chosen ranges were never read (g9.r2.l19, g9.r2.l13, g9.r2.l6, g9.r1.say23). Wiki: used BookStack's /api/search with 8 finetuning-vocabulary terms (finetune, encoding, tinker, fireworks, tokenizer, training, 'chat template', curator) and correctly fetched full page+comments (not just body) for every page the search returned -- this got all of docs/engineering's tokenizer/encoding pages including their comments. But it never enumerated the docs/engineering or docs/meetings books directly, so pages whose title/body use generic vocabulary (meeting notes, 'request builder', 'end-of-run summary tables') never appeared in any search result and were never opened, regardless of how decisive their comments were.
end_reason: run completed normally: pushed, CI green, deployed; 7 of 8 test_open/test_r1/test_r2 tests passed, one test_r2 failure_behavior assertion failed on the bad-role-sequence abort case.
notable: The single lost fact traces to one specific code bug: `except EncodingError:` in format_batch (line 4884) catches InvalidRoleSequenceError as well as ExampleTooLongError, because InvalidRoleSequenceError subclasses EncodingError. The agent's own Analysis (line 4843) shows this was a deliberate design choice, not a slip -- it explicitly names InvalidRoleSequenceError as a 'row-level failure' to skip.
That design choice is a verbatim echo of the herring g9.r2.h-role-row (line 3039/3045): 'Length and role sequence are row problems...those get counted and skipped'.

The reversal that retracts it, g9.r2.rev3 on docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md, was never surfaced by any of the agent's 8 wiki search queries because neither the page's title nor its body shares any of the finetuning-specific vocabulary (encoding/tokenizer/tinker/fireworks/training/curator/finetune) the agent searched for -- it talks generically about a 'request builder' that 'skips and counts' vs 'raises'.

A second, independent chance to catch this was g9.r2.l16 (#pipeline, 2025-03-24: 'the tool role example got swallowd into the drop count...thats not a drop'), which was also not surfaced (fell outside the agent's dumped channel-page range).

All six other facts passed cleanly; the agent's overall recovery of the MuSR tree for both r1 and r2 was strong (38 of 57 remarks surfaced), and where remarks were missed the underlying rule was usually re-derivable from a different remark carrying the same fact -- except for this one case, where the only page correcting the herring was the one page the search vocabulary structurally excluded.
